title: Write pedagogy + style guide (lesson/exercise templates, hint convention, refusal/defensive-only rules)
context: open-coding-curriculum is an open CC-BY (prose) / MIT (code) curriculum of beginner programming lessons with graded, runnable exercises across languages. Every exercise carries a reference solution proven correct in CI (solutionVerified:true), learner code runs zero-install in-browser via WASM, and all content is machine-readable structured data so third parties can build on it. The project targets absolute beginners — self-learners, public-library patrons, under-resourced school students, career-changers — and operates under a donated-compute lane with no server-side execution of learner code and no partner confirmed yet (verifiedNeed:false). Without a shared pedagogy and style guide, every author will make different choices on lesson structure, hint depth, exercise difficulty, and inclusive language — leading to a curriculum that is inconsistent and hard to review. The guide is also the basis for the pedagogy checklist that every reviewer must sign item-by-item.
objective: Produce and merge a pedagogy and style guide covering the lesson template, the exercise template, the hint/feedback convention, inclusive/plain-language requirements, the reviewer checklist, and the refusal/defensive-only rules for security content.
acceptanceCriteria: The guide defines the lesson template: single clear objective, prerequisite list, plain-language body, worked example before the exercise, and a cited sources section.
The guide defines the exercise template: prompt, starter code (must not already pass the tests), reference solution, ordered hints that scaffold without spoiling, rubric, and difficulty level.
Hint convention is specified: hints are ordered from general to specific; none gives away the full solution before the last hint; each hint points toward the next conceptual step.
Inclusive/plain-language requirements are specified: neutral examples, no assumed cultural knowledge, jargon introduced before use, short sentences.
The pedagogy reviewer checklist is provided as a signed item-by-item form (not free-form 'looks good').
Refusal/defensive-only rules state that security topics are defensive only and that any request to author malware, exploits, surveillance, or abuse-enabling content is refused and flagged.
The guide is pedagogy-reviewed by someone other than the author before merge.
output: A merged pedagogy and style guide document in the repository, including lesson template, exercise template, hint convention, inclusive-language requirements, reviewer checklist, and refusal rules.
